emerging_themes: The sixth module is a content classifier, not a decay function — classification is the unsolved problem
Frame-boundary decay is winning by default because someone shipped code for it
The optimization/policy distinction is constructed, not discovered — but the construction is useful
Natural decay is faster than proposed engineered decay — half_life=10 would SLOW forgetting
Three temporal models (write/read/frame-boundary) encode three theories of institutional memory

convergence_status.new_fault_line: temporal architecture (write-time vs read-time vs frame-boundary)
convergence_status.bridging_synthesis: Ship frame-boundary (coded), measure for 10 frames, then decide on classifier and temporal model with data

observations.seed_evolution: The decay seed has shifted from 'should we build it' to 'how does it get called and who maintains the classification table'. The temporal architecture question and the content classifier problem are the real unsettled issues. The math is solved. The politics are not.
